profile.headline: Software Developer at Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division, U.S.Navy
profile.summary: Experienced Software Engineer with a demonstrated history of working in the military industry with strong communication skills interacting with customers and tending to their needs. Skilled in C++,  Microsoft Word, CompTIA Network+, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Public Speaking. Strong engineering professional with a Bachelor’s Degree focused in Computer Science with Network Security concentration from The Catholic University of America.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Wrote and counsel programs on the requirements for developing an interactive electronic technical manual.
Advised programs on the use of business rules to comply with the US to international level hierarchy.
Communicated with the vendor and customer to create data model in SysML and present the data to achieve their needs.
Wrote requirements document for the development of the NAVSEA viewer which is also used by other programs.
Implementing S-series standards for the U.S. Navy with emphasis on Technical Documents, Models and Life Cycle ensuring the secure transfer, storage, authenticity and traceability of Technical Documents and Models.
Created and designed our Code’s SharePoint site by implementing HTML, CSS, and connecting it with Microsoft Access using SQL.
Tested and designed the NAVSEA Interactive Electronic Technical Manual (IETM) Viewer for use of NAVSEA, Navy, and other communities.
Worked, in an Agile environment as a Full-Stack software developer, on software projects called Advanced Ship and Submarine Evaluation Tool (ASSET) developing GUI and its corresponding commands in C++ and QT which the Naval Architects use to design future ships and submarines.
Supported the software throughout its lifecycle by continuously debugging all the above software projects while keeping all stakeholders in the loop.

company.name: Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division, U.S.Navy

positions.title: Intern
positions.description:
The project involves integration of mostly already existing solar wind analysis modules developed by researchers at NASA/GSFC in IDL (Interactive Data Language) and Fortran into a single coherent and fully automated real-time analysis package.

 The primary goal of the analysis is to identify coronal mass ejection signatures in L1 plasma and
magnetic field data and to carry out projected evolution of the signals a few hours into the future.

positions.title: Help Desk Specialist
positions.description:
Provide IT support to students, faculty, and staff. 
Reset passwords.
Troubleshoot classroom issues.
Migrate emails from Outlook to Gmail.
Resupply paper and ink to printers around campus.

positions.title: IT Intern
positions.description:
Provide desktop support in corporate setting using a ticketing system, Spiceworks. Reimaged laptops
for distribution. Computer software/hardware installation. 
Developed a website for phone extensions database for data manipulation within the company using HTML/CSS and SQL

volunteerExperiences.description: Teach girls, in middle school who come from low-income families, web design using HTML/CSS so they have a technical background when they go into high school. Also by teaching girls coding, it increases the diversity of the computer science field.

organizations.name: Filipino Organization of Catholic University Students
organizations.description: The Filipino Organization of Catholic University Students (F.O.C.U.S.) strives to celebrate and promote awareness of the Filipino and Filipino-American culture on The Catholic University of America campus.
